wheel.offset: ET63 on the 18x7.5 fitment (later 2015 G 550 factory 18s are ET43)
wheel.lug_torque: 96 lb-ft (130 N·m) — figure from the 2013–2015 US G-Class operator's manuals

max_tire.note: Fits an unlifted G 500 on factory 18s per Expedition Portal owners; a 285/65R18 rubs slightly at full left lock, and an ET63 aftermarket wheel rubbed where ET43 G 550 wheels didn't. Re-code the tire size so the speedo and ESP agree.
JWO 2-in and Eurowise 60 mm springs are sold as 33-in setups; JWO says keep wheel offset at +30 or lower (about a 30 mm spacer on most stock wheels) and fit longer shocks.
GwagenParts' ~75 mm front kit claims room for 35s; spacers may be needed to stop rubbing, and the kit includes caster-correction bushings.

JWO 4-in springs: offset no higher than +20 (typically a 50 mm spacer on stock wheels), caster-correction bushings required; adjustable panhard bars and a steering stabilizer recommended. Distronic likely won't work at this height.

items.title: Front turn signals behind grille cover don't meet FMVSS 108
items.summary: The grille cover over the front indicators can cut their visibility over time; dealers fit improved turn-signal units.

items.title: Incorrect software calibration (SCN) coding after a workshop visit
items.summary: Wrong coding could affect fuel gauge, check-engine light and speedometer, and stop the fuel pump cutting off in a crash; dealers recode.

timeline.change: G 500 launches with the 5.0-litre M113 V8 — the first regular-production V8 G
Not sold by Mercedes in the US; Europa International federalised G 500s and sold them with US VINs
G 500 Classic special edition marks the G's 20th anniversary — 500 built
Update brings ESP, Brake Assist and the 4ETS traction system; Mercedes-Benz USA starts official sales for the 2002 model year

Early US trucks have the electrical gremlins: Handsome Motors lists seat motors and controls, window regulators and motors, door-lock actuators and transfer-case actuators. Expedition Portal owners say the same about 2002–03
Grand Edition: 500 G 500 and G 55 AMG trucks for the US

The sweet spot. Handsome Motors says the early electrical faults got better every year and were mostly gone by 2005–06. 2005–06 trucks keep the simpler five-speed 722.6; 2007–08 trucks get the seven-speed 7G-TRONIC, HID lamps and a reversing camera

June 2006 production: the seven-speed 7G-TRONIC (722.9) replaces the five-speed 722.6 (ADAC). In North America that is the 2007 model year, which also brings HID headlamps, a reversing camera and tire-pressure monitoring
Three-bar grille; last US model year for the G 500 name
Replaced in the US by the G 550 with the 5.5-litre M273 V8

identify.intro: G 500s get dressed up as AMGs, and the early trucks came through three different doors — Europa International, grey imports and Mercedes-Benz USA — so check the paperwork, not the badges.

items.head: US VIN
items.body: Mercedes-Benz USA G 500s (2002–2008) start WDCYR49E; NHTSA's decoder reads that as a G-Class with a 5.0-litre engine built in Graz. Position 10 is the model year and position 11 is X for the Graz plant. A 2003 G 55 AMG reads WDCYR46E instead.

items.head: Europa trucks
items.body: 1998–2001 trucks sold by Europa International carry US VINs issued by Europa, not Mercedes. NHTSA's decoder flags one BaT-sold 2001 G 500 Europa VIN (WDBEG4213Z7122501) as non-standard, so expect the import paperwork to tell the story.

items.head: Fake AMGs
items.body: Bumpers, flares, wheels and badges bolt straight on, and Autocar warns about Gs converted to look like AMGs. Check that the VIN and factory data card agree with what's on the tailgate.

items.head: Factory data card
items.body: Mercedes-Benz Classic sells a digital vehicle data card for most passenger cars built 1986–2010 (AMG models excluded). It lists the model, original option codes, paint and trim, costs €130, and requires proof of ownership.

items.head: Gearbox
items.body: The five-speed 722.6 ran until June 2006 production; the seven-speed 722.9 (7G-TRONIC) followed, which in the US means 2002–2006 model years are five-speeds and 2007–2008 are seven-speeds. Check the VIN model year, the build month on the door-jamb label, and the dipstick: the 722.6 has one, the 722.9 does not. That matters for fluid specs and service intervals.

items.head: Three lockers
items.body: All three locks are worked from the dash buttons and engage in sequence: centre, then rear, then front. If a light won't go solid, suspect the vacuum side before the axle.

capability.note: braked; KBB lists 7,000 lb for the 2002 G 500

values.intro: On Bring a Trailer, prices have barely moved since 2018: the 2002–2008 G 500 is the cheapest way into a V8 W463, so condition and records matter far more than the year.
values.note: Based on 55 sold Bring a Trailer auctions of 2002–2008 US-market G 500 wagons from January 2025 to October 2026 ($18,500–$80,500, median about $35,000), plus four G 500 Cabriolet sales from 2024–26. Documented low-mileage trucks sit at the top; 2005 Grand Editions have sold for $34,500–44,200 in that period.

paragraphs: Mercedes only sold the G 500 in the US from the 2002 model year. Earlier trucks either came through Europa International, which federalised them and issued US VINs, or arrived later as grey imports. NHTSA lets any vehicle at least 25 years old in, counted from its date of manufacture, so a European-market G 500 or G 500 Cabriolet built before late 2001 can now be imported under Box 1 of the HS-7 form. Check your state's titling and emissions rules before you buy one abroad.

production.intro: The G 500 was a regular-production model, so it's the special editions that carry the numbers.
